subject: Migrating to Azure Marketplace billing — Nimbus Data next steps

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Migrating to Azure Marketplace billing — Nimbus Data next steps

Hi Sophie,

Thanks again for the time last week — really appreciate the transparency on your pricing cadence and how finance wants to centralize marketplace billing. Based on our conversation, I pulled together a short migration proposal that outlines the commercial mapping from your direct contract to Azure Marketplace billing plus recommended next steps for a smooth transition.

Key points up front:
- We can mirror the effective unit pricing for the remainder of your current term to avoid any cost shock.
- Marketplace consolidation typically takes 4–6 weeks (procurement approval + marketplace listing + billing cutover).
- Co-sell enablement on our side requires a brief partner contact form + an eligibility review — we handle the engineering onboarding.

I attached a concise proposal and an onboarding checklist (see attachments). If procurement is game, we can set up a 30-minute handoff with your procurement and our marketplace specialist.

Proposed next step: 30-min call with procurement + legal to confirm billing dates and any marketplace-specific invoice terms. Are you available Thursday 11/5 at 10am PT?

Attachments: Nimbus-Azure-Marketplace-Proposal-v3.pdf, azure_marketplace_onboarding_checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Subject: Re: Migrating to Azure Marketplace billing — Nimbus Data next steps

Marcus —

Thanks for the proposal and the checklist, those are helpful. A few quick notes from procurement/finance intercept so we can be efficient:

1) We need to confirm the effective date the marketplace invoice takes over for our FY accounting. Ideally we’d cut over at the start of a month to keep reconciliation simple.
2) Any change to payment terms? Our preferred cadence is Net 45; direct contract is on Net 30 today.
3) Are you able to keep the committed seat price for the initial 12-month window so our finance team can approve the transition without renegotiation?

Carl (cc) is our procurement lead — I’ll let him coordinate availability. Procurement would prefer a short MOP (mutual action plan) that lists milestone owners.

Also, worth noting we have an existing Azure marketplace account but not integrated for co-sell. We will need help on the co-sell enablement steps you mentioned.

Best,
Sophie Grant
Head of Cloud Operations | Nimbus Data
sophie.grant@nimbusdata.com

Thanks Sophie — appreciate the clear asks. Short answers below and I’ve sketched a proposed MOP in the attached SOW excerpt + checklist.

1) Effective date: We recommend aligning the billing cutover to the first of a month; if your team confirms a target month we’ll map proration in our billing system so you only pay net new Marketplace invoices from that date.
2) Payment terms: We can keep Net 30 for the first 12 months while your finance updates policies; if procurement insists on Net 45 we’ll need a brief finance review (we’ve found the marketplace vendors often accept Net 45 once the ISV has a direct billing agreement with the marketplace).
3) Price hold: Yes — for the initial 12-month transition window we can hold the committed seat price as outlined in section 2 of the proposal.

Next steps I propose:
- Carl/procurement provides target cutover month (EOD 11/6)
- Redwood to send DocuSign SOW addendum for the billing transition (we’ll include the price hold clause)
- Handbook call (30 min) for Azure marketplace enablement and co-sell kick-off

I’ve attached a condensed SOW fragment and the onboarding checklist again. If that works I’ll have our contracts team send the DocuSign link by end of day.

Attachments: Nimbus-Azure-Marketplace-Proposal-v3.pdf, Nimbus-SOW-signed.pdf, azure_marketplace_onboarding_checklist.xlsx

—
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
